title: Reuse rate estimation from sampled traces (sampling + de-biasing notes)
content:
Purpose:
Capture an analysis approach for estimating effective KV cache reuse rates from production traces that are sampled (not full-fidelity). The goal is to produce a reproducible estimator and quick diagnostics we can run nightly to detect regression in reuse (which drives paging / NVMe amplification).

Background / motivation:
- Full request traces are high-cardinality (token-level keys, KV touches) and expensive to store. We already sample 1:100 requests for full trace dumps and 1:1000 for lightweight telemetry. Naive reuse-rate estimates from these samples are biased: sampling probability depends on request size, route (customer/model), and time-of-day.
- We need a robust method to estimate the fraction of cache hits (reuse) per request or per-token that corrects for this sampling bias and provides CIs. This will be used to:
  * correlate reuse drop to eviction/paging increases;
  * trigger investigations when reuse degraded beyond threshold;
  * feed into the admission/pinning heuristics later.

High-level approach:
1) Stratified sampling: group traces by (route, model, seq_len_bucket) and compute sampling probability for each stratum from the ingestion logs.
2) For each sampled trace, compute raw reuse metrics (per-request reuse fraction, per-token first-touch flag, inter-request reuse distance when possible).
3) Apply inverse-probability weighting (IPW) at the stratum level to estimate global reuse rate and produce bootstrap CIs.
4) Run a small simulator to validate estimator under synthetic skew and burst scenarios we expect in production.

Important definitions (for this doc):
- reuse_rate_request = (#requests with at least one KV hit) / (total requests)
- reuse_rate_token = (total KV hits across tokens) / (total tokens observed)
- stratum = tuple(route, model, seq_len_bucket) where seq_len_bucket = {<=32,33-128,129-512,>512}

Sampling pipeline details (practical notes):
- Sampling metadata needed per trace: sampler_seed, sampler_rate, ingestion_ts, route, model, seq_len. We must ensure ingestion pipeline writes sampler_rate into trace header (some traces currently missing this). TODO: follow up with Observability team (Slack thread linked).
- Compute stratum-level p_s = observed_sampled_count_s / total_ingested_count_s as the empirical sampling probability for the period (use daily windows). For very small strata (n<50/day) fall back to parent strata (route+model or route-only).

Estimator (informal):
- For each sampled trace i in stratum s with observed reuse metric y_i, compute weight w_i = 1 / p_s. Then the weighted estimator for reuse_rate is: R_hat = sum_i w_i * y_i / sum_i w_i.
- For token-level reuse, y_i is token-level hits summed for trace i divided by token_count_i, and we weight similarly.
- Use a stratified bootstrap: resample traces within each stratum with replacement, recompute R_hat, repeat 2000 times to get percentile CI. This preserves per-stratum variance.

Bias sources and mitigations:
- Non-random sampling correlated with reuse: e.g., we intentionally oversample large requests. IPW corrects for this assuming p_s estimated accurately. If p_s is estimated poorly, bias remains. Mitigation: recompute p_s from ingestion logs and compare to expected sampling config; flag strata where discrepancy > 20%.
- Left-censoring: traces dropped before full KV phase (e.g., truncated) result in undercounting hits. Mitigation: mark truncated traces and either impute using similar nontruncated traces or exclude and report coverage.
- Temporal nonstationarity: reuse can vary intra-day. Use rolling 6-hour windows and produce both daily and 6-hour estimates; anomalies often show up faster on 6-hour windows.
- Multicollinearity of strata: if route and model always appear together, strata will be sparse. Mitigation: hierarchical pooling (empirical Bayes) in future iteration; for now we collapse to route-level.

Lab setup + runs performed so far (notes):
- Dataset: sampled traces from 2026-02-01..2026-02-28, sampling config: 1:100 for full traces, 1:1000 lightweight. We used only the full-trace sample.
- Stratification keys: (route, model, seq_bucket). Computed p_s from ingestion logs (daily).
- Quick numbers (preliminary):
  * naive average (unweighted): reuse_rate_token = 0.36, reuse_rate_request = 0.58
  * IPW estimator: reuse_rate_token = 0.28 (95% CI 0.26-0.30), reuse_rate_request = 0.51 (95% CI 0.48-0.54)
  * Interpretation: oversampling of long chat sessions (higher raw reuse) produced optimistic naive estimate. After de-biasing, per-token reuse is lower -> consistent with small infrequent requests causing most misses.
- Correlation with NVMe ops: daily series shows reuse_rate_token down by ~6 percentage points on days with 2x NVMe read amplification. Leads look plausible.

Simulator validation (what we ran):
- Synthetic workload generator that emits requests with known per-stratum reuse probabilities and sampling rates. We validated IPW recovers ground truth within Monte Carlo error for n>1000 total sampled traces; performance degrades with heavy stratification (lots of tiny strata).
- Edge-case: when a heavily reused tiny-stratum exists (p_s large but true population tiny), IPW variance exploded. Handled by capping weight at max_weight = 1 / min_p (default min_p=1e-4) which reduced variance but introduced small downward bias. Flagging needed.

Immediate next experiments / TODOs:
- Add ingestion pipeline writes for sampler_rate into every trace (missing for ~8% of traces). Blocker for productionizing this metric. (Owner: Jonah)
- Implement nightly job that computes per-route and per-model reuse estimates + CIs and uploads to the rollout dashboard. Use 6-hour and daily windows. (Owner: María)
- Test hierarchical pooling: implement simple Empirical Bayes shrinkage across seq_len buckets to stabilize small strata. (Owner: Devansh)
- Add a metric for weight distribution (histogram of w_i) and fail the job if 95th percentile weight > 1000.
- Investigate threshold rule for alerting: candidate rule = drop of >4pp (percentage points) in reuse_rate_token over 24h with p<0.01 by bootstrap. Need to tune to reduce false positives.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Should we prefer token-level or request-level reuse for alerts? Token-level is more closely tied to read amplification, but noisier. Request-level is more stable but less sensitive.
- Are we comfortable capping weights? Is there appetite for hierarchical modeling instead? (tradeoff: implementation vs statistical purity)
- Can we capture cold-start artifacts (new model versions) that temporarily inflate misses? Might need a separate tag and exclusion rule.

Appendix: quick sampler pseudocode (implementation sketch)
- Input: sampled_traces table with columns (trace_id, route, model, seq_len, tokens, kv_hits, sampler_rate, ingestion_ts)
- Group by stratum s = (route,model,seq_bucket) and compute p_s = sampled_count_s / total_count_s from ingestion log table
- For each sampled row i: y_i = kv_hits / tokens (token-level); w_i = 1 / p_s
- R_hat = sum(w_i * y_i) / sum(w_i)
- Run stratified bootstrap: for b in 1..B: for each s resample n_s rows with replacement, compute R_hat_b; compute percentiles.

Notes to self: keep this lightweight and pragmatic. The engineering cost to get a reasonably unbiased daily indicator is moderate; full hierarchical Bayesian pipeline is nicer but can wait behind the ingestion fix and alerting plumbing.

Linked artifacts: see JIRA-4532 for task breakdown, PR github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/commit/fe12a4b contains the prototype code used for the February run. Slack thread has a few logs where Jonah noticed missing sampler_rate headers.
